mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed, weekday trips fall and retail visits stay suppressed; that should keep RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both below baseline and weaker in t-0w than in t-3w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A further one-week drop in TRANSIT below the current weak level signals renewed access restrictions or avoidance, which then reduces discretionary shopping within 1-2 weeks and pushes RETAIL_REC lower.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 for a weekly mean after already being below -20
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -10.4 at t-3w to -23.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if a TRANSIT weekly mean below -25 is not followed by lower RETAIL_REC within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain weak, people substitute toward at-home activity and postpone discretionary shopping; RETAIL_REC then stays below its recent average over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive in every week while WORKPLACES is negative in every week
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and WORKPLACES stays below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility captures outdoor leisure substitution; if PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks, some discretionary trips shift away from malls and shops, lowering RETAIL_REC with a lag of about one month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -20 after being below -30
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was -31.1 at t-0w after -25.0 at t-1w and -31.0 at t-2w
failure_condition: Reject if a park-mobility rebound above -20 does not precede weaker RETAIL_REC within four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized decline in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT indicates broader mobility suppression, and that joint shock reduces retail browsing and impulse purchases over the next one to two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is near zero or negative while TRANSIT is sharply negative at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not weaken within one week after simultaneous declines in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both recover while TRANSIT remains soft, weekend local trips replace formal commuting and support neighborhood retail; RETAIL_REC should improve over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM each rise by at least 5 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both improved at t-1w relative to t-2w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both post week-on-week gains of at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline for several weeks, households consolidate activity at home and reduce discretionary outings; that persistent home-centered regime keeps RETAIL_REC below its last-four-week average over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive in all four weeks and peaks at 10.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline throughout that period.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve from their current troughs, it implies normalization of movement networks; that recovery should lift retail visits within four weeks as commuters add discretionary stops.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise by at least 5 points from their current weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both materially below baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean within four weeks after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise by at least 5 points.
